story_type: medicine airdrop to a fishing boat far offshore
hook: 675 miles from land, the captain needed medicine.
narration: Six hundred seventy-five miles from land, a fishing captain needed medicine.
He had severe pain and a fever, aboard the seventy-eight foot Sea Angel.
A Coast Guard Hercules from Air Station Barbers Point flew out over open ocean to find him.
That far out, a helicopter cannot reach you. So the plane drops supplies by parachute, and the boat steers to pick them up.
The fishing boat came around, rolling in the swell.
The crew leaned over the rail with a hook and caught the line.
outcome: They hauled the antibiotics aboard. Two days later a helicopter flew the captain to Hilo, in stable condition.
title: Medicine dropped 675 miles from land
description:
A Coast Guard HC-130 crew from Air Station Barbers Point airdropped antibiotics to the fishing vessel Sea Angel about 675 miles northeast of Hilo, Hawaii, in May 2025, after its captain fell ill. A helicopter later hoisted him closer to shore.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Avery Tibbets and Air Station Barbers Point, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/961814/coast-guard-medevacs-captain-fishing-vessel-offshore-hawaii

facts.claim: HC-130 crew airdropped antibiotics to a fishing vessel 675 miles offshore Hilo
facts.source_quote: An HC-130 Hercules airplane crew from Coast Guard Air Station Barbers Point conducts an airdrop of antibiotics to a commercial fishing vessel 675 miles offshore Hilo, Hawaii, May 7, 2025.
The 68-year-old captain of the fishing vessel had been reportedly experiencing symptoms including severe abdominal pain and fever.
from the captain of the 78-foot Sea Angel, which was about 675 miles northeast of Hilo
